Explain how a CPU and GPU differ, in about 150 words.

message.content:
CPUs and GPUs are both processors, but they are designed for different tasks. A CPU (Central Processing Unit) is optimized for speed and handles complex, sequential tasks with low latency. It has a few powerful cores that execute instructions one by one, making it ideal for general-purpose computing, running operating systems, and handling tasks that require deep logic or branching.

In contrast, a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is designed for parallel processing. It contains thousands of smaller, less powerful cores that can perform the same operation on thousands of data points simultaneously. This architecture makes GPUs vastly superior for tasks involving massive parallelism, such as rendering graphics, video editing, and machine learning. While a CPU excels at doing a few things very quickly, a GPU excels at doing many things at once, which is why it is the standard for high-performance computing and modern gaming.
